notes.note: Line counting is not observable in TTCN-3; the test only checks that CR LF and CR LF CR LF VT terminate line comments. That CR LF counts as one line (rather than two) is not covered.

Uses all 11 modifiers in their BNF positions. Titan has no @abstract template modifier and no @control function modifier (both are valid per the A.1.6 BNF: TemplateDef AbstractModifier and FunctionDef ControlModifier). Titan also reports that @decoded redirects are unsupported in its load-test runtime. These warnings are Titan limitations.
The requirement is a list; the reject test uses one listed word ('configuration') as an identifier. Titan accepts it because Titan does not reserve the extension-package keywords.
Restrictive reading chosen: value list notation used for a union type (not in the allowed list) is rejected.
Violation: enum template extension e_b(?) on an enumerated value without any associated value.
Permissive reading chosen: positive test using index assignment notation for record of, set of, array and map types.
Reading 1 chosen (integer required except for map keys); the test uses a float index for a record of type, which is invalid under both readings.

Positive reading: ? length(2) used inside a bitstring concatenation (same form as example 1 of clause 15.11). Titan does not support concatenating templates that contain matching symbols, so its warning is a Titan limitation.

A WildcardLengthMatch outside a concatenation normally parses as ExtraMatchingAttributes. The test uses '? length(1) length(1 .. 2)', where the first length can only be a WildcardLengthMatch outside a concatenation.
Reading 1 chosen: complement used as an operand of a bitstring concatenation. Complement is also excluded by clause 15.11, so the choice holds under both readings.
The truncated rule is read as 'string length shall be 1'; the test uses two-character bounds.
f_a(p_x := ?) with an in value parameter is invalid per this rule and clause 5.4.2. Titan accepts it, so Titan does not implement this check for named actual parameters.
